---
title: "check-redundant-citations.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags a source cited twice in one div or passage.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-19) is to cite a source once per div or passage,
at the claim it supports.
A second citation of the same source adds a number
that the reader must look up again and tells them nothing new.
This implements
[gha#1105](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1105).

A div or passage is the text between two `:::` lines or slide breaks.
The check flags a citation key that occurs twice in one such block
with the same locator, or with none.
Two kinds of citation count:

- **A bracketed citation.**
  Every key in `[@key]`, `[@key, p. 5]` or `[@a; @b, p. 5]` counts,
  including a citation that spans lines.
- **A `Source:` line.**
  Every `@key` on a line that starts with `Source:` counts,
  unless it sits inside brackets on that line, where it is already counted.

The check does not flag:

- an in-text citation (`@key [p. 5]` or `@key recommend ...`),
  because the author is the subject of the sentence;
- the same key with a different locator, which cites a different part of the source;
- the same key in different list items, because each item is its own claim;
- a cross-reference (`@def-`, `@eq-`, `@fig-` and the like),
  a code fence or a chunk option.

## Scope

Only repeats that touch a line a pull request adds are reported.
The whole file is parsed,
because the first citation can sit far above the added one.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.
Every run prints how many lines, files and blocks with a citation it examined.

The check warns by default, because the same key twice is sometimes right,
for instance the same book with the same locator for two separate claims.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default               | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd *.md'`        | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`                  | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`               | Fail the workflow when a source is cited twice in one div or passage. The default only annotates. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`               | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`              | Python version to set up. |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-redundant-citations.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a source cited twice, with the same locator, in one
# div or passage on lines a PR adds. Cite a source once per div, at the claim it
# supports. Warns by default; in-text citations and different locators are
# never flagged.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check redundant citations

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-redundant-citations.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                    # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                             # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-redundant-citations.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-redundant-citations.yml)
for the full caller stub.
